artifacts.summary: Ten-phase burn-down of all 348 all-target compiler warnings to zero, gated by a build-free trace-scan ratchet (scripts/warning-budget.py + C28) landed before the first fix, with a dedicated read-and-disposition phase for the 35 previously unanalyzed Tests/BimodalTest + exe-root warnings.

next_steps: Run /implement 585 to execute the plan, starting with Phase 1 (warning-budget scanner and all-target baseline).

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, CI invokes `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --no-build`, so any new numbered check (C1..C28) that shells out to `lake build` silently joins C2/C6/C24 in the documented 'Known Not-in-CI Gaps' list -- it passes locally and never runs on a PR. A gate intended to run in CI must therefore be build-free. For measurement gates over compiler output this is cheap rather than limiting: Lake stores each module's messages in `.lake/build/lib/lean/**/*.trace` as a JSON `log[]` array with a `level` field and replays them on a cache hit, so a pure trace scan reproduces the full warning surface in ~0.05s with no `lake` invocation, versus ~6s for a warm all-target replay build. Two guards are mandatory for such a scan: drop entries whose source path no longer exists (stale traces from deleted/renamed files), and exit non-zero -- never pass -- when no trace files are found or when a recorded non-zero baseline meets an observed zero, because a gate that silently measures zero is worse than no gate. Also verify the highest live check ID before numbering a new check: this harness is numbered past what its own header comment and external reports assume.
